newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia oil/gas receipts seen down till '98 - MIER.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia oil/gas receipts seen down till '98 - MIER.

text.p: Malaysia's receipts from crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) are seen falling until 1998 after a strong growth this year, the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said on Tuesday.

Export unit value of Malaysian crude oil is estimated to "average at a high $21" per barrel in 1996 due to low stocks in the U.S. during the cold winter months, the MIER said in its review of Malaysia's various economic sectors.
But the price is expected to moderate to $18.80 per barrel in 1997 when Iraq re-enters the market, and stabilise at $19 in 1998, the MIER said.
Export earnings from crude oil rose 4.8 percent in the first nine months of 1996 over same 1995 period.
Earnings from January to September 1995 were 1.0 percent higher compared to the same period in 1994.

The LNG export unit value is expected to be "at a relatively stable price of 332 ringgit per tonne in 1996", MIER said. The price is expected to moderate to 320 ringgit in 1997 and 1998, the institute said.
Earnings from LNG rose 45.6 percent in the first nine months of 1996 compared to a growth of 15.3 percent over the corresponding period in 1995.
